parsed.main_gap: Final answer (n+1)/(2n+1) is wrong (correct value is 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1)); the claimed lower-bound construction fails and no upper bound is proved.

errors.description: Wrong final answer. The proposed c=(n+1)/(2n+1) is not achievable for n=2: with Liu's own suggested cuts (0.4,0.4,0.2), Xiang uses a SINGLE cut splitting the 0.2 piece into 0.1+0.1, giving pieces {0.4,0.4,0.1,0.1}; Liu then gets only 0.4+0.1=0.5 < 0.6. The parity-changing option of using fewer than n cuts is never analysed.
errors.quote: So seems this construction guarantees at least 3/5.

errors.description: The 'invariance' lemma is proved only under the assumption that Xiang splits every big piece exactly once (2n+1 pieces). The claim that all other Xiang responses are at least as good for Liu is asserted from two hand-checked examples, never proved — and is in fact false.
errors.quote: But we also need to consider other Xiang strategies that do not split each big piece exactly once. We argued they give Liu at least as much. Need to prove best response for Xiang among all allowed splits is indeed to split each big once (any way).

errors.description: The upper bound (that Xiang can hold Liu to the claimed value) is entirely absent; the write-up explores several ideas, refutes its own grid-completion plan, and ends with an unexecuted plan to brute-force n=2.
errors.quote: So need different Xiang strategy to upper bound.

parsed.notes: Only the n=1 case (c=2/3) is genuinely settled; that value coincides with the correct general formula 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) at n=1. Text is explicitly exploratory ('Status: partial') with conjectures and pending computations.
